scope: Four nominal-mu PPO train/deploy cells, using the frozen new 400 Hz / action-rate -0.5 training recipe.
interpretation: The two native-family nominal deployments have similar core XY RMSE (0.128 m and 0.120 m), but this is not a statistical ranking or proof that contact is stable.
Transfer degradation is asymmetric for these two checkpoints. PhysX-trained to native CPU MuJoCo has 0.156 m core XY RMSE, whereas MJWarp-trained to PhysX has 0.573 m and 84.2% speed retention.
These observations include the whole closed-loop systems. They do not isolate a contact-law, actuator, integration or hidden-solver-state cause.
MuJoCo validation here is native CPU MuJoCo, not the GPU MJWarp training runtime.
The historical 200 Hz contact-reward replacement negative remains a separately labelled experiment; it is not a fifth matched cell in this new 400 Hz cohort.
